attributes.residual: Unchanged from baseline: real 72, insns 133/133, opcode multiset IDENTICAL (0t), frame 0xD0 both, saved-register set identical (stmw r21 in both). NAMED MECHANISM, now fully characterized and strictly sharper than the legacy cap: (A) a callee-saved GROUP SWAP. Target allocates in pure definition order - r22=index*916, r23=gEnemies base, r24=index, r25=oldc, r26=newc, r27=hitWorld, then the locals r28=startNode, r29=hint, r30=result, r31=node. Ours allocates the LOCALS to the low half (r23=hint, r24=result, r25=startNode, r26=node) and the PARAMETERS to the high half (r27=base, r28=index, r29=oldc, r30=newc, r31=hitWorld). The two contiguous groups are simply ranked in opposite order; live ranges, instruction positions and opcodes are identical in both builds, so nothing in the source distinguishes them. (B) ONE adjacent independent instruction swap at the StartItemGrid call: target emits `mr r3,r26` then `fmr f1,f27`, ours the reverse. EVIDENCE that (B) is a CONSEQUENCE of (A) and not a separate source fact: MWCC emits call arguments in strict ARGUMENT-INDEX order at both other call sites in this same function (CritterCollideStart at 0x64 and the 7-argument CritterMoveNodeCol at 0x74 are each byte-aligned and index-ordered), and the StartItemGrid prototype order is ground truth - dyngrid.c:197 DEFINES `void StartItemGrid(f32 r, f32* pos)` and include/game/dyngrid.h declares it - so the reversed order cannot be spelled in portable source. WEBFRANK ASSESSMENT: NOT eligible as configured. The existing enemy.c pins use copy_register_fields, which recolors registers but cannot REORDER instructions; residual (B) is an instruction permutation, so a copy_register_fields pin would leave the function non-exact. Closing (B) by source first would make the remainder a pure renaming bisimulation and hence a strong pin candidate, but no source lever for (B) exists per the argument-index evidence above.
